commitMessage:
Bug 545261 - [12][quick assist] Split case expressions/statements.

Locate the statement index of the selected node's SwitchCase and copy
all its statements (they'll be the subsequent statements up to and
excluding the next SwitchCase), inserting them before the original
SwitchCase along with the newly created SwitchCase representing a single
label. This is done for every label of the original SwitchCase.
Afterwards the original SwitchCase and its statements are removed.

- This applies to JLS12 or higher, where the selected ASTNode is the
'case' keyword (eg. SwitchCase) or a label of the 'case' expression (eg.
element whose parent is a SwitchCase)
- The ordering of the SwitchCase labels is preserved
- Add AssistQuickFixTest12 for testing this quick assist

Change-Id: I3fd37046b63622174a46ff20ebff43205b5d18ea
summary: Quick assist to split multi-label switch cases into individual cases, reorganizing statements.

commitMessage:
Bug 547502 - Improve performance of Chain Completion feature

- Note that Chain Completion remains fully disabled
- Stop re-computing bindings for the invocationSite (IJavaElement) type
- Computation that discounts candidate entry points by comparing whether
they match the completion prefix can be performed earlier on the
IJavaElement (using getElementName()) as opposed to on the IBinding
(using getName())
- When resolving bindings for Java type elements (IType), the parser can
skip method bodies for faster parse times
- Make the chain finding functionality time out after 1 second and
include the findEntryPoints() logic within that execution
- When a potential chain completion entry point is a :
  -- Java type element (IType), only resolve its bindings if it contains
     any public static non-void members
  -- Java method (IMethod), or Java field (IField), only resolve its
     bindings if it is non-void, non-primitive
- Bump jdt.core.manipulation version

Change-Id: Iacc46878fc9fe7487a72ae4c9129e7e5455a2e8c
summary: Updates the default value for the `PREF_CHAIN_TIMEOUT` preference from 3 to 1.

dslRule:
<!id: fix.varargs.array.warning>
<!description: Explicitly cast an array to Object[] when it is the last argument passed to a varargs method to fix a compiler warning regarding ambiguous varargs usage.
This ensures the array itself is treated as the varargs parameter, not that its elements are extracted into individual arguments.>
<!severity: WARNING>

$receiver.$method($args$, $arrayExpr) :: instanceof($arrayExpr, "java.lang.Object[]")
=> $receiver.$method($args$, (java.lang.Object[]) $arrayExpr)
;;
summary: Adds an explicit `(Object[])` cast to an array expression when it is the final argument of a method call that uses `Object...` varargs, resolving potential compiler warnings.
